correctness.rationale: Using pair B=(1-1/h)S where S has weight one, the recursion gives hQ=L+h-1, so h(K_X+B)=-LS is Cartier. Toric positivity shows this pair is klt, and index control forces A_(X,B)(v)∈(1/h)Z_{>0} for every divisorial v, giving A_X(v)>=1/h+(1-1/h)v(S). If center lies on S, choose some chart U_j, for which aj S is Cartier: v(S)≥1/aj≥1/a1; outside S smooth A^n has A_X≥1. On chart at p1, primitive quotient vector (1,a2,...,an)/a1 has age (1+Σ_{j>=2} aj)/a1 = 1/h+(h-1)/(h*a1), realizing equality. Strict inequality aj<a1 for any other chart U_j on S, j>=2, forces p1 as unique center, not unique valuation. Previously proved Bie–Du–Yu volume asymptotic plus h*mld→1 gives the normalized limit. Independent rational cyclic-quotient ages checked n=2,h=3..9 and n=3,h=3..4 (including uniqueness of the minimizing chart/group element); infinite claim relies on toric discrepancies and Cartier index, not these examples.
